name: Oirase Gorge (奥入瀬渓流), Yakeyama to Lake Towada
why: Fourteen kilometres upstream beside a clear river in beech forest, past mossy boulders, rapids and a dozen waterfalls, to the outlet of Lake Towada.
book: Free and open all year, no permit. JR buses from Aomori and Hachinohe stop at Yakeyama and along the road beside the river (Ishigedo, Choshi Otaki, Nenokuchi): ride back or cut the walk short. The road is jammed at the autumn leaves in mid to late October: come by bus.
water: Toilets and drinks at Yakeyama, Ishigedo and Nenokuchi only. Carry 1 litre.
dangers: Wet roots and stones on the path; falling branches after storms.
Asian black bears live in the forest: stay on the path and make some noise.
In winter the path is under snow and only partly walkable: ask at the Oirase Stream Museum.
turnaround: None needed: the road and its bus stops run beside the whole walk. Plan to reach Nenokuchi before the last bus.

points.name: Yakeyama
points.note: The hot spring village at the bottom of the gorge, with the JR bus stop and the Oirase Stream Museum (maps, bike rental). Walk upstream: the light and the falls face you.

points.name: Ishigedo
points.note: Rest house with toilets about 4 km up. Above it come the best stretches: the Ashura rapids and the Kumoi falls.

points.name: Choshi Otaki falls
points.note: The one waterfall across the whole river, a wide curtain that kept fish out of Lake Towada. Bus stop by the road.

points.name: Lake Towada, Nenokuchi
points.note: Where the river leaves the caldera lake: bus stop, toilets and the pier of the lake cruise boats to Yasumiya.
